methodology.summary: Patterns are aggregated from third-party email-pattern/lead-generation tools (RocketReach, LeadIQ, SignalHire, ContactOut, AeroLeads, NeverBounce, Mailsfinder, Clay, and similar), plus occasional first-person forum reports (Blind, Glassdoor, Quora). This is NOT verification against actual known employee mailboxes -- no individual address was tested for deliverability.

confidence_scale.high: Most or all independent tools checked agree on the same dominant pattern, generally with consistent reported prevalence.
confidence_scale.medium: A plausible primary pattern exists but sources disagree meaningfully, or only one or two sources were available.
confidence_scale.low: Sources disagree substantially on the dominant pattern, or there is direct evidence the company does not enforce a single format.

important_caveats: These lead-gen tools frequently disagree with each other about the SAME company's dominant pattern -- sometimes by 40+ percentage points, or naming an entirely different pattern as #1. This is a limitation of the whole industry, not unique to this dataset.

Large companies commonly run multiple valid formats simultaneously (legacy aliases, acquired-company domains, regional differences, employee-chosen aliases), so a 'dominant' pattern is a probability, not a guarantee for any individual.
None of these have been confirmed by Anthropic or Claude against a real, currently-working mailbox. Treat every entry as a well-sourced guess, not a verified fact.

This data should not be used to construct bulk/mass outreach to individuals who have not consented to contact. Guessed-address spam has a high wrong-person/bounce rate and, more importantly, reaches people who never opted in.
